parakeet: What happens when entire societies stop asking questions? When sermons replace science, means replace arguments, politics replace values, and likes replace logic. Imagine waking up and realizing most people around you don't question anything anymore. The world got louder, faster, and so saturated with takes that the human mind evolved for inquiry, discernment, growth, slid into passive acceptance. What happens to a society when thinking is replaced by instant reactions, surface opinions, and echo chambers? This is about how critical thinking is disappearing and why collective stupidity spreads without anyone noticing. By the end, I want to hand you something simple but urgent, a way to reclaim your mind and a system designed to keep you comfortably numb. It dares to ask the one question today's environment can't stand. Is this really true? And in a society obsessed with being right, even asking is treated as a threat. Now they're rare. And without them, analysis shrinks into reactions, reflection collapses into scrolling, and understanding gets replaced with opinions. Not that we know less, but that we've lost the space to think deeply about what we know. So what do we actually lose when critical thinking fades? It begins with the courage to say, I think differently. If collective stupidity spreads through shortcuts and certainty, how do we turn the ship?
